steps.label: Scratch Skills Recap
steps.content:
Year 6 Scratch

Scratch Skills Recap

Year 6, 6.2.4.5

  • Control a sprite with the keyboard, using x and y.
  • Keep score with variables and decide with if.
  • Change costumes, backdrops and levels with messages.
  • Build two games that check themselves, ready to plan your own.

steps.label: Keyboard Control and the Grid
steps.content:
Keyboard Control and the Grid

The player controls a sprite with events. The sprite moves on a grid of x and y.

  • x runs from -240 (left) to 240 (right). y runs from -180 (bottom) to 180 (top).
  • when [key] key pressed runs its script each time that key is pressed.
  • change x by (15) moves right. A negative number moves left.
  • Anything that happens all game long goes inside a forever loop.
when flag clicked
go to x: (0) y: (-140)

when [left arrow v] key pressed
change x by (-15)

when [left arrow v] key pressed

steps.label: Variables and Decisions
steps.content:
Variables and Decisions

A variable stores a value that changes while the game runs. An if block decides what happens next.

  • set a variable when the green flag is clicked, so every game starts fresh.
  • change it during the game: +1 for a catch, -1 for a miss.
  • A comparison such as (lives) = (0) is true or false.
  • if then else runs the top part when true and the else part when false.
when flag clicked
set [lives v] to (3)

change [lives v] by (-1)
if <(lives) = (0)> then
say [Game over]
stop [all v]
end

steps.label: Check: Variables and Decisions
steps.content:
Check: Variables and Decisions

Choose the best answer.

items.prompt: lives is 1. The player misses once more and change [lives] by (-1) runs. Which condition is now true?
items.explain: 1 take away 1 is 0, so (lives) = (0) is true and the game can end.

items.prompt: Which block should run when the green flag is clicked, so every game starts with 3 lives?
items.explain: set gives lives an exact value. change would add to whatever was left from the last game.

steps.label: Fruit Catcher Toolkit
steps.content:
Fruit Catcher Toolkit

Blocks for the next challenge. Work out where each one goes.

go to x: (pick random (-200) to (200)) y: (170)

if <(y position) < (-170)> then
change [lives v] by (-1)
end
  • pick random gives a different number each time, so the Apple drops from a new place.
  • y position < -170 is true when the Apple reaches the bottom: a miss.
  • A catch is touching [Bowl]?.
  • When lives reaches 0 the game is over.

steps.label: Activity 1: Fruit Catcher
steps.content:
Activity 1: Fruit Catcher

Work on your own. The starter project has the Bowl and the Apple.

Build it

  • The arrow keys move the Bowl. The green flag sets score to 0 and lives to 3.
  • The Apple starts at the top at a random x, then falls.
  • A catch adds 1 to score. A miss takes 1 from lives. Either way the Apple goes back to the top.
  • When lives reaches 0 the game ends.

The panel beside TurboWarp lists the checks. Press Check my project as often as you like: it plays your game and tells you what it saw.

steps.label: Costumes, Backdrops and Messages
steps.content:
Costumes, Backdrops and Messages

Costumes bring a sprite to life. A new backdrop and a broadcast make a new level.

  • next costume inside a loop, with wait (0.2) seconds, animates a sprite.
  • switch backdrop to [Level 2] changes the stage picture.
  • broadcast [level up] tells every sprite at once, and every when I receive [level up] script starts.
if <(score) = (5)> then
broadcast [level up v]
end

when I receive [level up v]
switch backdrop to [Level 2 v]

steps.label: Check: Costumes and Messages
steps.content:
Check: Costumes and Messages

Choose the best answer.

items.prompt: A walk animation changes costume far too fast to see. Which block fixes it?
items.explain: A short wait inside the loop slows the costume changes down.

items.prompt: Which block starts a script when a message arrives?
items.explain: broadcast sends the message. when I receive waits for it.

steps.label: Activity 2: Level Up
steps.content:
Activity 2: Level Up

Work on your own. The Hero already moves with the arrow keys.

Build it

  • The green flag sets the backdrop to Level 1, score to 0 and level to 1.
  • Touching the Coin adds 1 to score and sends the Coin somewhere new.
  • At 5 coins, broadcast level up.
  • Receiving level up switches to Level 2, sets level to 2 and the Hero says Level 2!

The panel beside TurboWarp lists the checks. Press Check my project as often as you like: it plays your game and tells you what it saw.

steps.label: What Every Game Needs
steps.content:
What Every Game Needs

Next lesson you plan and build your own game. The My Game checker looks for these six parts.

SpritesAt least two: one to control, one to catch, dodge or collect.
Controlswhen [key] key pressed, or set x to (mouse x).
A loopforever keeps things moving and checking.
A variableSet at the green flag, changed during the game.
A decisionAn if block with touching or a comparison.
An endingstop [all], say [Game over], or a new backdrop.
